_comment: Battlefield terrain types. A TYPE is a rule, not a look: how fast a body of men crosses this ground, whether it can cross it at all, how much cover it offers and how much of a sight line it stops. Terrain is simulation data first - the battle reads these numbers and the visual layer is generated from the same cells. Soil (data/terrain/soils.json) and biome (data/terrain/biomes.json) are the other two axes: a cell is a TYPE crossed with a SOIL inside a BIOME, and the movement multiplier the battle finally reads is composed from all three at generation time - see BattlefieldTerrain._resolve_move(). Adding a type is a row in this table, not a code change.

_fields.id: stable key, written into the per-cell type array
_fields.name: what a player would call it
_fields.description: one line, for the debug overlay and for whoever adds the next biome
_fields.move_multiplier: how much of a unit's speed survives crossing a cell of this type (1.0 = nothing lost)
_fields.traversable: false means no formation may stand or walk here; the traversability map is built from this, from slope and from obstacles
_fields.cover: 0..1, how much protection the ground itself gives a soldier standing in it
_fields.los_blocking: 0..1, how opaque this ground is to a sight line drawn across it (a wood is a thicket, not a wall; a cliff is a wall)
_fields.colour: debug overlay colour only - the renderer draws art, never this

terrain_types.name: Open ground
terrain_types.description: Clear, level ground. Nothing in the way of a formation.

terrain_types.name: Rough ground
terrain_types.description: Broken, tussocked earth that slows a body of men without stopping them.

terrain_types.name: Light woods
terrain_types.description: Scattered trees. Ranks cannot keep their dressing in here, and a sight line through it is a guess.

terrain_types.name: High ground
terrain_types.description: Rising ground that takes the sting out of an uphill advance.

terrain_types.name: Mud
terrain_types.description: Water standing in the soil. Men cross it slowly and ranks come apart in it.

terrain_types.name: Water
terrain_types.description: Deep enough that no formation crosses it. A river is a wall with a current.

terrain_types.name: Cliff
terrain_types.description: A rock face. Nothing formed crosses it, and it stops a sight line dead.
